unit.why: A short narrative about the tzaddik foreseeing his death, secretly dictating his last will to a scribe on Hoshana Rabba, and the will being revealed only after his passing.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a series of numbered death-related anecdotes; the deathbed scene follows in the next division.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מפי מגידי אמת כי בשנה
stories.summary_en: On Hoshana Rabba before his death, the tzaddik secluded himself with a scribe, dictated his last will, revealed that he would die soon after the festival and swore the scribe to secrecy; the scribe left weeping and produced the will only after the tzaddik died.

tags.why: The story is about the last will and the approaching death of the tzaddik.

quotes: וגילה לו אז כי בקרוב אחר החג יסתלק לעולמו
tags.why: He foretells his own death, and the prediction comes true.
The narrative arc is a prediction of his death that is fulfilled.

quotes: בהושענא רבא אחרי גמרו ההושענות והתפלה
tags.why: The scene is set on Hoshana Rabba / Sukkot.
The tzaddik's death is the event the story leads to.
The festival prayers are mentioned as the moment before the scene.

quotes: ודמעתו על לחייו בעינים אדומים מרוב הבכיה
tags.why: The scribe weeps over the coming death; this is grief, not melancholy as a spiritual problem.
The story is framed as heard from trustworthy tellers.

missing_concepts: scribe or secretary who is not a sofer
